description: The USGS documented unplugged orphaned oil and gas well dataset, called DOW, lists the location and status of unplugged orphaned wells across the United States as of 2022, produced with the Department of the Interior after the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. It holds 117,672 wells in 27 states with coordinates, American Petroleum Institute number or other identifier, well type, well status and explanatory notes. Wells count as orphaned when the state says so or when they have had no production for an average of 12 months, are unplugged, have no responsible party and have a documented location. The data were requested from state oil and gas agencies or downloaded from their databases, with coordinates derived using Bureau of Land Management and state tools where missing and no other manipulation. Access: free download under a CC0 public domain marking, with a companion data report and an online map. Coverage is 27 states, with gaps where states do not document orphaned wells. Caveats: the count is a documented minimum as of 2022, and definitions vary between states. It suits hazard exposure and capacity planning studies of legacy oil and gas wells, and relates to the orphaned oil well imagery record catalogued here.
